A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TCAS study despite the changed title and organization. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and supplied appendices are readable and support reliable comparison. v2 lists an Appendix C that is not present; no substantive content is inferred from that listing.

before.justification: v1 reports original attention analyses, intervention experiments, TCAS versus SFT evaluations, hyperparameter studies, and qualitative examples across the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds duration-stratified results, random-intervention comparisons, and finer hyperparameter sensitivity results.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same head selection, timestamp aggregation, token filtering, contrastive loss, and combination with next-token prediction. v2 explicitly explains that TCAS does not require ground-truth temporal labels for its auxiliary loss, but this clarifies the existing algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Charades and ActivityNet grounding and consistency benchmarks, TimeIT and VTune training annotations, and Charades-derived EOJ probing dataset. The new duration analysis subdivides existing Charades-CON cases rather than introducing another population, dataset, or task.

E2.justification: v2 Table 8 introduces random attention intervention as an evaluated comparator alongside SFT, ground-truth intervention, and TCAS. The benchmark comparator sets remain unchanged. Qwen2.5-VL and Video-LLaMA grounding rows move from v1 Table 4 to v2 Table 9 rather than being removed.

E3.justification: New analyses introduce four duration bins containing 58, 189, 409, and 51 cases, random-intervention strengths of 0.05, 0.1, and 0.15, and finer t and thr grids. Table 8 additionally evaluates interventions using the existing sample-wise IoU-product consistency metric. Settings for the retained benchmark experiments are unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds duration robustness analysis in Section 5.5/Table 6, random-intervention controls in Appendix B.3.2/Table 8, and finer sensitivity sweeps in Appendix B.6/Figure 16. These extend the existing diagnostic studies; the original attention visualizations, correlations, EOJ analysis, intervention sweep, and case studies remain.

E5.justification: The Pearson correlations, regression analyses, distribution summaries, and significance-reporting practices are retained. The p-values newly displayed in v2 Section 3.2 already appeared in v1 Appendix A.2. Neither version documents repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or seed-based variability.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark scores remain unchanged. New Table 6 reports grounding scores of 58.8 for SFT versus 76.5 for TCAS on videos longer than 40 seconds. New Table 8 reports rephrase/shift consistency of 65.4/33.1 for SFT versus 70.0/37.5 for TCAS, with additional intervention results. Figure 16 adds sensitivity results. v1's explicit EOJ correlation coefficient of 0.447 is omitted, although its plots remain.

T1.justification: The cross-modal, discriminability, and EOJ score definitions retain their mathematical substance. v2 Equation 4 formalizes the attention mixing already described in v1, while EOJ notation is clarified. No substantive theorem, proof, derivation, or formal assumption is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction soften temporal consistency from a bottleneck to an important factor in temporal understanding. The conclusion drops the broad SOTA grounding and consistency claim. The central contributions concerning attention discriminability and TCAS remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 attributes grounding gains to regularization that suppresses language-prior shortcuts and explains limited intervention gains through frozen components that cannot co-adapt. Appendix B.4 newly qualifies grounding benefits for Qwen2.5-VL and Video-LLaMA as inconsistent or small. The conclusion explicitly limits the work's coverage of broader temporal understanding.

D1.justification: v2 specifies the A100's 80GB memory and documents the intervention's convex mixing formula and uniform ground-truth attention target. Appendix B.3.2 clarifies metric usage across analyses and comparisons. These are added disclosures; the stated optimizer, learning rate, batch size, frame counts, resolution, and training duration remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 expands discussion of modality-specific circuits and image-language alignment, adding RexTime, transformer-circuit, LLaVA interpretability, and language-prior/modality-bias references. TimeLogic and AnetQA citations are removed. These refine the motivation and mechanism discussion while retaining the original positioning around internal attention analysis.

P1.justification: Most prose is retained, with localized rewrites and reorganization: the title and author block change, Related Work moves after the introduction, the standalone generalizability subsection is condensed, and method, metric, discussion, and conclusion passages are revised. The expanded appendix outline also lists a Section C absent from the supplied document.

P2.justification: The document undergoes extensive reformatting of page geometry, typography, spacing, and caption placement. EOJ heatmaps move into the main text while their violin plot moves to the appendix; the grounding comparison table is split between main text and appendix. Figure 9 gains red outlines, and Tables 6 and 8 and Figure 16 introduce new displays.

improvement.justification: The added intervention controls, duration analysis, finer sensitivity results, and metric explanations modestly strengthen support for the unchanged method. Narrower grounding claims and explicit applicability qualifications better reflect the retained benchmark evidence. The new shortcut-suppression explanation is not directly tested, and the absent Section C remains an editorial gap, limiting the overall gain.
